changes.statement: dct:description The DALICC deontic dependency graph with default rules for what a licence does not say, under the law of the European Union: moral rights that cannot be waived in Austria, Germany and France, the sui generis database right, the mining exceptions of the Digital Single Market Directive, decompilation for interoperability and exhaustion after a first sale. The graph is complete: it holds the axioms and the adopted rule of the core graph beside its own rules, and it is built from the core graph and a difference file. Each rule names its legal basis and says in plain words what it does. The rules are proposals until the association's legal reviewer adopts them. Nothing in this graph is legal advice.

The explanations of the rules were reviewed against the statutes they cite; seven were corrected: the Austrian moral-rights rule names what section 19(2) of the Urheberrechtsgesetz voids and what section 20 leaves to agreement; the French rule cites the Code de la propriété intellectuelle with its accents; decompilation is allowed within the limits of article 6 of the Software Directive, and a prohibition is reported by eu-interop-void instead of being read as removing the exception; resale follows Tom Kabinet (C-263/18) for works and UsedSoft (C-128/11) for software; the database right names the lawful user's right to insubstantial parts (articles 8(1) and 15 of the Database Directive); the mining rule reads a prohibition in the licence as a reservation under article 4(3) and recital 18 of the Digital Single Market Directive; and the research mining rule names cultural heritage institutions and the purpose of scientific research. The description says that moral rights are national law, which EU law does not harmonise. The adopted endorsement rule of the core graph cites its basis, says that only a use suggesting endorsement is refused, and names who adopted it. Follows core graph version 3.
